messages:
maria: Heads up, seeing a recurring NVLink/link flap on rack23-gpu-07 starting ~08:12 UTC. 99p token latency spikes on hosted inference routes that map to that host. Possible AER/Xid correlation.

maria: quick dmesg snapshot (filtered):
```
[ 248912.123456] pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id=00e0
[ 248912.123457] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 248913.001234] nvlink0: link 1 down
[ 248913.001567] nvlink0: link 1 up
```

dmitri: which rack/node exactly? 65:00 looks like slot 3 on that host, right? can you paste `nvidia-smi -q` for GPU 0/1? also ping the infra-bmc team for any recent BIOS updates. :eyes:

samira: pasting minimal `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,uuid,serial,driver_model.current,temperature.gpu --format=csv` output for node:
```
index, name, uuid, serial, driver_model.current, temperature.gpu
0, A100-SXM4-80GB, GPU-abc123, SNR12345, WDDM, 42 C
1, A100-SXM4-80GB, GPU-def456, SNR12346, WDDM, 45 C
```

samira: journalctl shows repeated Xid 31/79 around the same window. no recent PCI rescan or driver reload.

ajay: we should drain the node and move pods off the affected GPUs. small production impact but safer. plan: cordon+drain gpu-rack23-n07, run hardware diagnostics, reseat riser, then put back. who can own the drain now?

maria: I can start the drain in 10m. want to try a non-invasive mitigation first: toggle persistence mode and disable NVLink peer access for gpu1 to see if latency stabilizes. commands I plan to run:
```
sudo nvidia-smi -i 1 -pm ENABLED
sudo nvidia-smi -i 1 --gpu-disable-peer-access
kubectl drain node/gpu-rack23-n07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
```

dmitri: please also capture `sudo ethtool -S pcie*` (we have a helper script /usr/local/bin/pcie-stats) and save full dmesg + `lspci -vvv` for the team. if reseat doesn't fix it, request RMA for that card (serial SNR12346).

oncall-bot: Incident created: INF-2026-0042 (severity: high) — assigned to eng-runtime oncall. Link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INF-2026-0042

samira: after draining, I ran quick stress on remaining GPUs in the rack and saw throughput return to baseline. disabling peer access on GPU1 removed the repeated nvlink link up/down for ~20m, but Xid entries still appear intermittently.

maria: hardware team says this riser was replaced 6 months ago; BIOS rev looks older than others in same rack. scheduling a maintenance window tomorrow 02:00 UTC to swap the riser and test with latest BIOS in the spare lane.

dmitri: note for capacity planning: node has 8xA100, taking it OOS for 2 hours will impact Dedicated customers if scheduled at peak. recommend moving some reserved workloads to backup pool and notify sales about possible SLA blips. adding cost estimate: ~0.9 GPU-hour lost per active customer shard (rough).

ajay: I'll open a sales-notify thread and mark Dedicated customers affected. Also add a postmortem checklist item to add NVLink link flap detection to our alerting (pattern: repeated nvlink link up/down + Xid within 5m).

samira: after reseat tomorrow we'll run synthetic NVLink stress (`nvlink_test --streams 4 --dur 10m`) + long-running inference load to validate. if it still fails, escalate to vendor for replacement.

maria: thanks team — draining now, will paste runbook steps and final diagnostics into this thread when done. :thumbsup:
